Title: Health Check Design Pattern
QuestionDetail: In Route 53's health check system, why do health checkers send dummy results even when there are fewer active health checks than maximum capacity?
AnswerDetails: Health checkers send dummy results to maintain a constant work pattern. This ensures network load and aggregator work remains constant regardless of customer configurations, eliminating a significant source of variance.
OptionA: To maintain constant network load and aggregator work
OptionC: To provide backup data if real checks fail

Title: Anti-Fragility in Systems
QuestionDetail: Which characteristic makes caches potentially problematic despite appearing anti-fragile at first?
AnswerDetails: While caches can improve response times under load, they have modes (empty vs. filled) that can cause response times to worsen significantly when empty, potentially leading to cascading failures.
OptionC: They are too slow to update

Title: Configuration Management
QuestionDetail: Why does AWS Hyperplane use S3-based configuration files instead of a workflow system for handling Network Load Balancer changes?
AnswerDetails: Using S3-based configuration files allows for constant work patterns where nodes fetch and process configurations regularly, avoiding slowdowns during high-change periods that would occur with workflow systems.
OptionA: To maintain consistent processing speed regardless of change volume

Title: Self-Healing Systems
QuestionDetail: What makes constant work designs naturally self-healing compared to workflow systems?
AnswerDetails: Constant work systems operate in 'repair everything' mode on each iteration, automatically correcting issues without building backlogs or requiring complex repair sequences.
OptionA: They start from a clean slate in each iteration
OptionB: They maintain backup copies of all data

Title: DNS Server Health Checks
QuestionDetail: How do Route 53 DNS servers handle health check status changes?
AnswerDetails: DNS servers receive fixed-size tables of health check statuses periodically and store them in memory. They perform the same operations regardless of status changes, maintaining constant work patterns.
OptionA: By maintaining consistent operations regardless of status changes
OptionB: By updating records only when changes occur
